0.comment: Odette: Violetta and the Spessiva family
0.content:
Violetta Spessiva comes from an old family of Korolevskiy ballerinas whose glory had long faded. Little remained but yellowing portraits in a draughty house and the family's classic ballet "Spirit Seeker". She was a demanding teacher: one misplaced foot meant starting over. When her husband died, she went back to rehearsals, collapsed onstage during a performance and was told she would probably never dance the hardest steps again. She went on teaching Odette from a wheelchair, beating time with her cane, and refused Signora's offer to take her daughter. Canon does not say she has died; Odette's old dream was to earn enough to support her.

Violetta danced "Spirit Seeker" herself but never taught it to Odette. In 7.0 Odette revived it for its first performance in years. Sandrone was unsure she was ready, and in the tomb vision Signora observed that every dancer makes the choreography her own. Odette says the same unspoken wound passes between mother and daughter whenever their eyes meet. Violetta once told her there was too little feeling in her dancing.

1.comment: Odette: Odette's father and the blurry photo
1.content: Odette's father, never named, was a Fatui soldier who smelled of leather and gunpowder and could not keep a beat. He applauded louder than anyone, let little Odette ride on his boots, touched her back and told her, "Back straight, little snow swan," and promised she would be a prima ballerina. He took a hopelessly blurred photo of her first full turn en pointe and kept it in his pocket watch. He died on duty early in what became Project Stuzha. Two Fatui soldiers brought the letter, and the watch came back stained with rust and blood. Odette has never forgotten the one line of that letter she glimpsed.

2.content:
Signora, Eighth of the Harbingers, was Odette's father's commanding officer. She came at Capitano's behest to offer condolences, noticed the girl's agility, and offered to take her into the Fatui with an allowance for the family. When the child insisted, she answered coldly, "Then come along. Let us see how long that resolve of yours lasts." Her training was brutal: cold, collapse, injury, illness, constant pressure to live up to the Fair Lady's name. Odette resented her and practised ballet in defiance. When Signora caught her one night, Odette said she did not deserve to watch the dance her mother had taught her. Signora said nothing, left, and never interfered again. Odette now says she is indebted to her.

On the night watch Odette asked the Traveler whether Rosalyne had left any last words; she had not. The Traveler passed on what Sandrone had said: Arlecchino had advised Signora, and Signora had gone to see Odette. Odette had not known Signora went to Mondstadt until after she left. Odette notes that Sandrone's tea parties always put Rosalyne in a softer mood.

3.comment: Odette: The Cor Ignis and the Sanctuary of Grief
3.content:
Signora gave favoured subordinates a Cor Ignis, her flame sealed in ice. It was a mark of favour, and she always knew where each one was. When she died, many crushed theirs with relief. Odette kept hers, because its warmth was one of the few sensations she still felt clearly. She lent it to Paimon as a cold remedy. At the Armory Palace, as the Curse of Death took her, she pressed it to the Traveler on a hunch, and it guided their soul back early.

After the crisis Odette went to Signora's ice-sealed tomb at the Sanctuary of Grief, a place she had never thought she would visit. In a cinematic she remembered Arlecchino handing her a letter: Signora's final words, sealed in a Cor Ignis that held the Knave's "Two Worlds' Flames" rather than Signora's own fire. Arlecchino said the choice was hers. Odette danced for her mentor, then shattered the ice with a dagger of ice. The freed flames burned the letter and vanished as crimson moths, and she walked away without looking back, choosing to live on as both ballerina and Fatuus.

4.content:
The Rokot is a non-violent, anonymous Snezhnayan organisation that serves ordinary people and opposes Project Stuzha. As "Lelek", Odette was its most infamous agent. Lelek slipped into guarded rooms leaving no trace, left threatening letters, and frightened corrupt elites into line; the press cheered "We stand with Lelek!" Industrialist Chugunov's unexpected vote against Stuzha was put down to Lelek. Sandrone and Tartaglia used Odette's skill as a benchmark, and Sandrone realised she fitted the profile and had a motive.

Snowed in at the theater, Chugunov blamed Lelek for two deaths. Confronted privately by the Traveler, Vodyanitsa and Alyosha, Odette said: "Yes, I'm Lelek, and no, I'm not the murderer." She then confessed in front of everyone, because otherwise the whole search would focus on Lelek, which was exactly what the real culprit wanted. She told any accuser to produce evidence or hold their tongue. Vodyanitsa was mortified she had never noticed. After the Armory Palace break-in, a Rokot notice, citing the harm Lelek's radical actions had done to the organisation's reputation, withdrew the codename permanently, announced that the Rokot had negotiated a waiver of her penalties, and suspended her, reminding members that motives and methods matter equally.

5.content:
The Korolevskiy Troupe's prima donna, a Water Imp, is one of the few people Odette speaks freely with. They met through backstage work: Odette calmed nervous newcomers with rehearsal logic while Vodyanitsa fired them up. Later Odette secretly gave Vodyanitsa her last honey candy "for your throat", not knowing a Water Imp's voice barely strains. Now Vodyanitsa packs three boxes of candy into Odette's bag and demands one back, swears she has caught her smiling, and makes her read fan letters. Odette says the smile was "simply the expression the role called for."

Before the Tsaritsa's first visit to a performance, Vodyanitsa pushed up the corners of Odette's mouth and made her repeat "What. Great. News." When ill, she clings to Odette's arm, which Odette allows because it does not hurt. She drags Odette to feed stray cats, which sharpen their claws at her. Vodyanitsa never suspected Odette was in the Rokot, let alone Lelek.

6.content:
Odette met the Traveler at the collapsing Svetloledovka mine, warned them off, then took them for the backup from Snezhnograd. Together they drove off a burrowing monster and evacuated five miners. She was startled when the Traveler criticised two Harbingers to their faces, and visibly shaken when Tartaglia revealed they had duelled Signora. At Zolnyy she told them it was no hard feelings and helped them buy and ship Kristall to the poor. She then came to Podvorye Restaurant with candy and her Cor Ignis for the ailing Paimon.

On the night watch she shared her past and, as a favour in return, told them what Stuzha's energy research was for. She thanked them for not exposing her as Lelek. When Pierro took Paimon, she led the Traveler to the Armory Palace and insisted on forcing her way in: "I may be a Fatuus, but I'm also Lelek." Afterwards she waited outside Glupov and was relieved to see Paimon well.

7.content: On a Fatui mission nearby, Odette heard of a collapse at the Svetloledovka mine and organised the rescue. She covered the rear while the miners escaped and posted warning signs afterwards. The episode kept troubling her; back at the theater she could not focus on dancing. She went to Zolnyy and, with Alyosha and the Traveler, bought up the available Kresnik Kristall, booking it as mission expenses and adding train carriages under Stuzha regulations, escorted by Fatui guards. She remarked that the state, not private citizens, ought to cover relief that is behind schedule.

8.content: After the "Spirit Seeker" rehearsal, a snowstorm trapped the audience in the Korolevskiy Theater, and people died night after night. In fact everyone was already in an afterlife shaped by Ronova's Curse of Death. Odette confessed to being Lelek, stood night watch with Valeriy and the Traveler, and found from the logbook that there was an extra person without a ticket (the ghost Shram). She told the Traveler she had seen Mitya dead in the Armory Palace a week earlier, and she realised that Chugunov's "Tonia" (Ptashka) was dead. When Ronova revealed herself, she killed Odette and Chugunov with a snap of her fingers. Everyone woke in their seats with no memory until reminded.

9.comment: Odette: Breaking into the Armory Palace
9.content: When Pierro took Paimon from Podvorye Restaurant, Odette guessed he had gone to the Armory Palace and led the way. The Traveler wanted to spare her, as a Fatuus, from trespassing; she said she would force her way in regardless. They fought past startled guards into the old structure beneath, while she asked the Traveler not to hurt researchers who didn't know they were intruders. When the Curse of Death struck, she used her Cor Ignis on the Traveler before falling. When she woke, she found she could not get past the guards alone, so she returned and waited outside. Mitya later named her the first witness of the curse. Soon afterwards the Rokot withdrew her codename.

10.content: Alyosha is a hunter who could live comfortably on hunting alone but takes odd jobs at the theater to help others, so Odette was not surprised he joined the Rokot. They work as a trio with Vodyanitsa: rescues, Kristall runs, the Seals of Life. In 7.1 he played a frail old man to lure out Avaz.
